APOLLO: 

“.. Imagine saying: ‘I will take you from New York to Los Angeles, but I'm not telling you how quickly, what it will cost or how you'll get there.’ By not explaining these important elements, you may question if we are actually getting to Los Angeles.” [Slok]

I almost entirely whiffed on the statement, my mockup yesterday. But maybe I wasn’t the one who whiffed?  What a disappointing Fed Day. bsky.app/profile/clau...
Note, the actual statement today (below) looked very little like my mockup. bsky.app/profile/clau...

The statement: a hold and 3 dissents—Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan wanted a hike now. That was the only info. No rationale for the hold, no hint at what a hike would take. Not one word of the data discussion changed after six weeks of inflation and jobs surprises. None, zip, nada. Never seen that.

Dissents in favor of a hike, if they happen, should earn the "hawkish hold" stamp, but without a rationale for the hold, no discussion of what could lead to a hike, or any hint of forward guidance, it might be a weak one.
I would argue 'the market' was also different in the Greenspan times. I am not sure the experiment Warsh appears to be running will work as well now.

Warsh wants markets to react to data, not the Fed. Whatever the Fed does today brings more surprise than usual. A little is manageable, but if markets misread the Fed's intent, it snowballs into pricing on future meetings. Not a disagreement about inflation; a disagreement about the Fed.

Markets almost always see the Fed coming. Each dot is a Fed meeting; the height shows the agreement in fed funds futures market about the decision. The rare close calls—lift-off in 2015, the 2019 tariff pivot, Sept 2024's 50-bp cut—were hard policy calls. This one is regime change.

The Fed decides today, and markets are unusually uncertain about what's coming. Hike odds were running near 30% yesterday. That's not normal; it's the second-most uncertain scheduled Fed meeting in 15 years. Video + thread: www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/...
The tortured sound in my voice here it’s real. Happy Fed Day y’all, may we be blessed with a boring one. www.marketplace.org/story/2026/0...
What do I see in the charts? Steady as she goes, largely.
